leading_positions.synthesis: Three members prefer targeted protein degradation (B014) as the whole prize, citing a new pharmacological principle (catalytic, event-driven removal of the target through E3 ligase recruitment), independent reproduction over two decades and an active clinical pipeline. They do not share a laureate trio: Aili and Aqvist name Crews, Deshaies and Handa, tying the PROTAC concept to the cereblon mechanism of thalidomide-type drugs, while Chabes names Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli, emphasising structure-guided VHL ligands and ternary-complex design. All three concede that Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto, Ito and Kim have serious claims and that no PROTAC is yet approved.

Three members prefer palladium-catalysed C-N cross-coupling (B046) with an identical two-laureate allocation (Buchwald and Hartwig, working independently with complementary ligand families). They share the case for mechanistic clarity, three decades of confirmation, daily industrial use and a clean credit. They share the same reservations: closeness to the 2010 cross-coupling prize and the unrewarded precursor work of Kosugi, Migita, Guram and Rennels. Citation wording differs only in small details (general, ligand-controlled).

One member (the chair) prefers Car-Parrinello first-principles molecular dynamics (B027) with Car and Parrinello, on grounds of unambiguous two-author credit, four decades of use and no overlap with the 2013 or 2024 computational prizes. The stated costs are limited appetite for another computational prize, a physics-flavoured image, and less visible day-to-day chemical impact. B027 is an explicit alternative for Aqvist, Brzezinski and Somfai.

One member prefers ionizable lipid nanoparticles (B060) with Cullis, Hope and Madden, citing lipid self-assembly physical chemistry, pKa-controlled charge and endosomal escape, and clinical validation through siRNA and mRNA products. The stated weaknesses are credit spread over at least six people (Anderson, Langer and MacLachlan left out), patent-driven priority disputes and overlap with the 2023 Medicine prize. B060 is an explicit alternative for Aili and Chabes.

areas_of_agreement: All eight preferred configurations are single-part prizes; no member proposes a split prize, so the three-laureate limit is binding in every file.
Six of eight members prefer either B014 or B046, and each of these two groups rests on independent confirmation over two or more decades.

B014 and B046 are each an explicit alternative for members who prefer the other: Brzezinski and Somfai list B014 as an alternative, and Aili's statement calls B046 a strong fallback on credit clarity.
Every member names attribution as the main weakness of their own preferred configuration, and no member claims the credit question is fully resolved.
Maturity and independent reproduction are accepted as the baseline requirement; members differ over whether clinical approval is also needed.
scientific_disputes: Whether Pd-catalysed C-N coupling (B046) adds a new concept beyond the 2010 C-C cross-coupling prize (Somfai, Zou and Brzezinski say yes, in the ligand-controlled mechanism; Aili treats it as methodology close to the 2010 concept and the same worry is registered in Brzezinski's own file), or only extends the same catalytic cycle to a new nucleophile.
Whether PROTACs and cereblon-type molecular glues form one principle (induced proximity to an E3 ligase, as Aili argues) or two separate achievements (as Zou and Chabes raise).
Whether first-principles molecular dynamics (B027) is chemistry of the weight of a reaction or drug modality, given its physics-flavoured framing and the 2013 and 2024 computational prizes.
Whether lipid nanoparticle delivery (B060) is a distinct chemical discovery or an engineering optimisation adjacent to the 2023 Medicine prize.
attribution_disputes: B014: the third place is contested between Handa (Aili, Aqvist; cereblon mechanism) and Ciulli (Chabes; structure-guided VHL ligands). Ito (joint cereblon paper with Handa), Gray, Sakamoto and Kim are left out of either trio, and Sakamoto's versus Ciulli's role in the founding concept is debated.

B046: all three supporters name Buchwald and Hartwig and leave out Kosugi (tin-amide coupling), Migita, and Guram and Rennels; they say this openly and rely on generality as the reason, which not every member has tested.
B060: the Vancouver trio (Cullis, Hope, Madden) versus the lipidoid and lipid-optimisation lineage (Anderson, Langer, MacLachlan); patent disputes limit what the scientific record can settle.
B027: no allocation dispute is stated, but the chair's file notes that Parrinello's later work (metadynamics, machine-learned potentials) could blur how his contribution is framed.
maturity_disputes: B014: no degrader is yet approved, although cereblon-based glue drugs are; members split on whether the clinical proof of the cereblon strand answers the objection for the PROTAC strand.
B046 and B027 are not disputed as mature (about three and four decades of independent use), but supporters of B014 hold that age alone is not the criterion.
B060: maturity is clinical and large in scale, but the opening ballots and member statements disagree about whether this is a chemistry or an engineering milestone.
B007 (phase separation) is not preferred by any member in round 1, but it is listed as an alternative by Sparr and questioned by Aili as unsettled in vivo.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Sparr discloses that she holds her B060 view as a lipid physical chemist and may overrate the lipid phase-behaviour side of the story.

Linke (chair) discloses that his B027 preference rests partly on recollection of the 1985 publication details and that the method is often described as physics-flavoured; this is a disclosed position, not a recusal.
No member's round-1 file declares a recusal or a formal conflict with any named candidate.
questions_for_round2: If B014 goes forward, should the third laureate be Handa or Ciulli, and can the committee write a citation that either covers both the PROTAC and cereblon strands or openly recognises only one?
Is the absence of an approved PROTAC a reason to defer B014, given that cereblon-based glue drugs are approved?
Does Pd-catalysed C-N coupling (B046) differ from the 2010 cross-coupling prize in a way that the committee can state in one sentence of citation?
If B046 goes forward, is excluding Kosugi, Migita, Guram and Rennels defensible on generality grounds, and how should that be stated?
Can B014 and B046 supporters say what evidence would move them to the other configuration, and would any member rank B027 or B060 above both?
For B027, is there appetite for a third recent computational prize after 2013 and 2024, and for B060, can the committee separate chemistry from delivery engineering?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows two three-member blocs (B014 and B046), plus single preferences for B027 and B060; B014 has two different laureate trios, whereas B046 has one. No ballot has the five votes of a majority. Merit, maturity and credit pull in different directions: B014 leads on novelty with the most open credit question, and B046 leads on credit clarity with the most open novelty question. Round 2 should resolve those two trade-offs rather than count the existing blocs.
